title: Coefficient compatibility of the tensor-map purity transpose
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $R=\mathcal O_E\subset S=\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sf-setting]. For $T=X,Y$, put $A_{n,T}=(R/\ell^n)_T$, $B_{n,T}=(S/\ell^n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site, and use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Write $\mathcal N_A(T),\mathcal N_B(T)$ for their normalized constructible subcategories with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], and $C_T=-\otimes^L_{A_{\bullet,T}}B_{\bullet,T}$ for scalar extension of whole systems [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Twists mean [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Write $P_A=Rf_{!,A,\bullet}\dashv G_A=f^!_{A,\bullet}$ and $P_B\dashv G_B$ for the specified tower adjunctions, with units $\eta_A,\eta_B$ and counits $\epsilon_A,\epsilon_B$ [det-sp-tower-gluing]. Fix the same compactification for the two compact-support functors [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Let $b:C_YP_A\xrightarrow{\sim}P_BC_X$ be the coefficient comparison formed by the proper direct-image coefficient mate followed by the open-extension tensor identification, as in [lem-sp-field-shriek-system-comparison]. Let $c_K:C_XG_AK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BC_YK$ be the $P_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $C_Y\epsilon_{A,K}\circ b_{G_AK}^{-1}$ [lem-sp-field-exceptional-system-comparison]. Put $J_A=(A_{n,Y})_n$, $J_B=(B_{n,Y})_n$, $\omega_A=G_AJ_A$ and $\omega_B=G_BJ_B$. For $K\in\mathcal N_A(Y)$ assume specified levelwise finite-Tor etale-origin witnesses for the pairs $(K,\omega_A)$, $(C_YK,\omega_B)$ and $(C_YK,C_X\omega_A)$, in the domain of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a). Let $\pi_A,\pi_B$ be the actual tower projection maps [def-exchange-projection]. Define $\tau_{A,K}:f_A^*K\otimes^L\omega_A\to G_AK$ as the transpose of
$$P_A(f_A^*K\otimes^L\omega_A)\xrightarrow{\pi_A(K,\omega_A)^{-1}}K\otimes^LP_A\omega_A\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{A,J_A}}K,$$
and similarly $\tau_B$. These are the specified tensor maps of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; at the coefficient unit they are identities of $\omega_A,\omega_B$ under unit constraints. Under scalar tensor and pullback identifications there is a tower equality
$$c_K\circ C_X(\tau_{A,K})=\tau_{B,C_YK}\circ(1\otimes c_{J_A}).$$
For the diagonal orientations $a_A,a_B$ of [det-sp-tower-gamma](1), the maps $\tau_A(1\otimes a_A)$ and $\tau_B(1\otimes a_B)$ are exactly the specified tower purity maps of that node, evaluating to [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Consequently, if $c_{J_A}C_Xa_A=a_B$ under the twist comparison, then
$$c_K\circ C_X\gamma_{f,A,\bullet}(K)=\gamma_{f,B,\bullet}(C_YK)$$
with the canonical pullback/twist source comparison. Both displayed equalities hold for actual morphisms of derived coefficient systems before taking limits. Their normalization is the counit transpose above, not a choice of a tower lift of finite maps.

proof.text: Work throughout in the ordinary derived categories of strict coefficient systems. By [lem-sp-field-scalar-normalized-systems], $C_T$ preserves the normalized constructible domain with its uniform bounds. By [det-sp-tower-gamma](2),(3), the objects $G_AK,G_BC_YK,\omega_A,\omega_B$ and the sources of the tensor transposes lie in the specified tower adjunction domains. The coefficient tensor and pullback identifications are actual natural system comparisons [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In particular $C_X(f_A^*K\otimes^L\omega_A)$ identifies with $Q=f_B^*C_YK\otimes^LC_X\omega_A$. The three supplied pairs of finite-Tor etale-origin witnesses allow [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels](2a) to invert precisely the three projection maps used below. No assertion about equality of maps is deduced from their evaluations.

proof.text:
Write $q_A=\pi_A(K,\omega_A)^{-1}$ and $q'_B=\pi_B(C_YK,C_X\omega_A)^{-1}$. Applying [lem-sp-field-projection-system-square] with $W=\omega_A$ and composing with the two inverse projection maps gives the equality
$$(1\otimes b_{\omega_A})C_Y(q_A)b_{f_A^*K\otimes\omega_A}^{-1}=q'_B.$$
Here and below scalar tensor and pullback comparisons are understood as in that node. The unit component of the counit equation in [lem-sp-field-exceptional-system-comparison] is
$$\epsilon_{B,J_B}P_B(c_{J_A})=C_Y(\epsilon_{A,J_A})b_{\omega_A}^{-1}.$$
These are equalities of system morphisms, with the same chosen compactification and the same specified coefficient mate $b$.

source.place: (2), tensor-map transpose; explicit whole-system counit calculation

proof.text:
Compare the two maps from $Q$ to $G_BC_YK$ under the Hom bijection of [det-sp-tower-gluing]. The transpose of $c_KC_X\tau_{A,K}$ is
$$\epsilon_{B,C_YK}P_B(c_K)P_B(C_X\tau_{A,K})
=C_Y(\epsilon_{A,K})b_{G_AK}^{-1}P_B(C_X\tau_{A,K})
=C_Y(\epsilon_{A,K}P_A\tau_{A,K})b_{f_A^*K\otimes\omega_A}^{-1}.$$
The first equality is [lem-sp-field-exceptional-system-comparison]; the second is naturality of $b$. Substituting the defining transpose of $\tau_A$ and the inverse projection equation from step 2 reduces this to
$$(1\otimes[C_Y(\epsilon_{A,J_A})b_{\omega_A}^{-1}])q'_B.$$
For the other map, let $q_B=\pi_B(C_YK,\omega_B)^{-1}$. Naturality of the projection transformation [lem-sp-field-projection-system-square] in its $X$-input gives
$$q_BP_B(1\otimes c_{J_A})=(1\otimes P_Bc_{J_A})q'_B.$$
Consequently the transpose of $\tau_{B,C_YK}(1\otimes c_{J_A})$ is
$$(1\otimes\epsilon_{B,J_B})q_BP_B(1\otimes c_{J_A})
=(1\otimes[\epsilon_{B,J_B}P_Bc_{J_A}])q'_B.$$
The unit-component counit identity in step 2 identifies these two expressions. Injectivity of the tower Hom bijection proves the first displayed equality of the statement. This is a counit computation inside the system category; finite evaluation is not used.

proof.text: At $K=J_A$, the projection map under tensor unit constraints is the identity of $P_A\omega_A$. Indeed its proper factor is the adjunct of the proper counit tensored with the coefficient unit [def-exchange-projection, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], hence is the identity by the adjunction triangle identity. Its open factor restricts to the identity under the open unit, and so is the identity under tensor unit constraints by the open adjunct characterization [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], which applies to strict ring systems. Thus the defining transpose of $\tau_{A,J_A}$ is $\epsilon_{A,J_A}$. Under [det-sp-tower-gluing] this is the transpose of $1_{\omega_A}$, proving $\tau_{A,J_A}=1_{\omega_A}$. The identical calculation for $B$ gives $\tau_{B,J_B}=1_{\omega_B}$.

source.place: (2), tensor-map transpose; explicit whole-system counit calculation

proof.text: By [det-sp-tower-gamma](2), the specified tower purity maps are exactly $\tau_A(1\otimes a_A)$ and $\tau_B(1\otimes a_B)$ after twist reassociation, and their finite evaluations are [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Precompose the equality proved in step 3 with $C_X(1\otimes a_A)$. Naturality of scalar tensor identifies the resulting middle composite as $\tau_B(1\otimes[c_{J_A}C_Xa_A])$. If the stated orientation equation holds, replace the bracket by $a_B$ to obtain $c_KC_X\gamma_{f,A,\bullet}(K)=\gamma_{f,B,\bullet}(C_YK)$ with precisely the canonical pullback/twist source comparison. All compositions took place before inverse limit. Evaluating the same identity at level $n$: by [det-sp-tower-gamma](1),(2) the level of $a_A$ is the inverse $\Pi_f^{-1}$ of the finite diagonal isomorphism and the level of $\gamma_{f,A,\bullet}(K)$ is $\gamma_{f,A_n}(K_n)=\theta_{f,K_n}(1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})$ after twist reassociation [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]; system tensor evaluates levelwise [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Since $1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1}$ is invertible, $(\tau_{A,K})_n=\theta_{f,K_n}$, the tensor map of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; likewise for $B$. This is the identification of $\tau_A,\tau_B$ with the specified tensor maps asserted in the statement.
